messages:
Alisa (Product): FWIW I pushed a short PRD draft for gen API edge behavior (streaming, truncation, token limits, retries). Link: https://redwood/s/PRD-gen-edge. Can folks enumerate acceptance criteria + must-cover edge cases for launch?

Devin (Eng): Thanks — will skim. High-level ask: define minimum deterministic behaviors for when we hit token limits and during retries (so customers can build fallback UX).

Marta (Eng-ML): Enumerating model-level edge cases that matter to acceptance: partial final tokens when truncated, stop-sequence split across chunk, function-call JSON getting cut in stream, KV cache mismatch after retry, and model temperature/state differences after a resumed stream.

Sam (Eng-Runtime): Runtime concerns: we must guarantee idempotent retry semantics for completed chunks vs in-flight tokens. Also need a resume token contract for streaming so client can request from offset N.

Lee (QA): Can we get a concrete test matrix? e.g., (1) stream cut at token limit mid-token, (2) stream cut on stop token boundary, (3) retry after connection drop with resume header, (4) user-supplied max_tokens smaller than model min-context => error path.

Noah (Customer Success): A customer (FinServe) reported a production case: streaming answer includes a function call that gets truncated; their app attempted to call the function with invalid JSON. They want "either complete the function payload or an explicit error token so we can surface a retry UI".

Devin (Eng): Acceptance criteria proposal (minimal):
- When truncation occurs due to model or request token_limit, API returns a deterministic truncation marker in streaming and final responses.
- If a function call is truncated, we must emit a structured stop reason ("truncated_function_payload") in the final event.
- Streaming resume tokens are supported for transient network failures within a short TTL (e.g., 60s).

Marta (Eng-ML): Add: truncation must not produce syntactically invalid function JSON by default. If it's unavoidable, we must annotate with an explicit field so downstream parsers can reject safely.

Sam (Eng-Runtime): Proposed resume token payload (opaque to user but stable):
```json
{
  "resume_token": "base64(kv_offset|stream_pos|model_variant)",
  "expiry": 1710000000
}
```
Client passes resume token as header: `X-Redwood-Resume: <token>`. If token invalid/expired, server responds with 409 + hint.

Lee (QA): Tests to write: fuzz truncated function JSON, validate explicit stop-reasons, ensure resume token replay doesn't duplicate tokens in final output (idempotency). Need automated harness + a small external client to exercise resume flow.

Devin (Eng): On retries: semantics boil down to 3 cases — (A) request never reached model (safe retry), (B) request reached model but no final event (partial output), (C) request completed server-side but client didn't ack. We should define server responses for each and a suggested client behavior.

Marta (Eng-ML): For case B we should prefer resume semantics (continue from last acked token) rather than full re-eval. But model state must be recoverable; we can only resume when we have prefix KV and same model_variant/quantization. If not, fall back to full re-eval with an explicit warning in the final metadata.

Noah (Customer Success): From product/cust pov: expose clear error codes and short docs: "TRUNCATED", "RESUMABLE", "NON_RESUMABLE" with quick examples — customers will build UIs accordingly.

Sam (Eng-Runtime): Implementation note: resume requires we persist per-stream prefix KV for TTL and ensure eviction doesn't happen during TTL. Memory/backpressure impacts for high concurrency — we'll propose a policy in the PRD.

Devin (Eng): Edge-case checklist for PRD (short):
- mid-byte/utf8 split when truncating => must not emit invalid UTF-8 (either backtrack 1 byte or indicate truncated).
- stop sequence spanning chunks => ensure we detect across chunk boundary.
- function-call JSON cut => emit `truncated_function_payload` + example partial payload in metadata.
- max_tokens smaller than prompt => 400 error with reason `insufficient_budget` (clearly documented).
- resume token replay after long delay => 409 conflict with `resume_expired`.

Lee (QA): Also add metrics/alerts: percent of streams ending with truncation (goal <1% by GA), percent of resume attempts that succeed, and top 5 failure reasons.

Marta (Eng-ML): Small model nuance: top-p / temperature should not dominate resume equivalence guarantees. If model isn't deterministic, clients should be warned — add `determinism_hint` in metadata (HIGH/MEDIUM/LOW) for each served variant.

Alisa (Product): This is great. Action items: (1) Devin + Sam write precise acceptance criteria section (deadline EOD Thu), (2) Marta + Lee create test vectors and fuzz harness (proto by Mon), (3) Noah draft FAQ snippets for CS by Mon. I'll consolidate into PRD and tag for review. @deploy-bot can you attach the current PRD link to this thread?

deploy-bot: Attached PRD draft https://redwood/s/PRD-gen-edge v0.3 (updated refs).

Noah (Customer Success): I'll collect two customer examples and add to PRD (FinServe case + internal pilot).

Sam (Eng-Runtime): One more runtime detail: when we choose to auto-truncate (server-enforced) vs reject with `insufficient_budget`, make auto-truncate configurable per-customer via plan flags. Add config flag `allow_auto_truncation` to PRD.

Devin (Eng): A request — make sure the API returns both machine-friendly `final_reason` fields and human-readable `final_message` so we don't force parsing for basic dashboards.

Alisa (Product): Thanks all. I'll draft the launch checklist items from this thread and post the updated PRD here when done.
